standard.title: Collect and organise observations
standard.description: collect, sort and record information and data from observations and from provided sources, including unscaled timelines and labelled maps or models
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y1 (AC9HS1S02): Students collected information from a range of sources and recorded on unscaled timelines and labelled maps.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students collect, sort and record information from observations and provided sources using unscaled timelines and labelled maps.

nodes.label: Collecting from historical and geographical sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collect relevant information from a range of sources appropriate to both historical and geographical inquiry, identifying relevant information for their purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect information from at least two different source types relevant to a Y2 inquiry (e.g. photographs and maps, or survey data and satellite images).
nodes.typical_width: Collect from: photographs, interviews, newspapers, stories, place/street names (historical); surveying peers, satellite images, field photographs, observations of monuments (geographical); identify relevant information from each source.
wider: Compare sources created at different times (e.g. a historical map and a current satellite image) and discuss what each reveals
Evaluate the reliability of different source types for a specific inquiry question
nodes.hinge_reason: Recording on timelines and maps requires prior collection of information — without collected material there is nothing to record.

response_modes.reason: Year 2 introduces geographical data sources (satellite images, field photographs, surveys) alongside historical ones — build familiarity with each source type through whole-class exploration.

success_criteria: Collects information from at least two source types
Identifies which information from each source is relevant to the inquiry question

nodes.label: Pictorial maps, timelines and location recording
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create pictorial maps with annotations, locate connected places on maps, and order events on unscaled timelines.
nodes.minimum_width: Complete at least one of: annotated pictorial map, location map of connected places, or ordered timeline of local community history.
nodes.typical_width: Create pictorial maps with annotations showing historical sites or connected places; locate places they are connected to on maps; order key events in local community history on unscaled timelines; use slideshows or story formats.
wider: Create a layered map that shows both historical sites and current interconnections for the same area
Compare an annotated historical timeline with a modern map of the same area and identify changes

response_modes.reason: Pictorial mapping and timeline creation integrate collected information, spatial understanding and time sequencing — both formats are the recording integration tasks.

success_criteria: Produces at least one annotated map or ordered timeline from collected information
Annotations accurately represent information from sources
